name: Shadowphone
tagline: A second, disposable phone number for texts and calls you would rather not attach to your real line.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The app layer here is genuinely thin: buy a number, route inbound SMS and voice to yourself, send from that number, keep threads in a database. An agent can build that in a weekend on top of a telephony API, and for a single person with one or two numbers it works fine. What you cannot one-shot is the telephony itself, because numbers come from carriers and messaging at any volume drags you into registration paperwork. So you end up with a real replacement that is permanently renting the hard part from someone else. The gaps are mobile: no native app, no reliable push, and MMS plus voicemail are each their own small project.
coreLoopDIY: Provisions a phone number from a telephony API, receives and sends SMS and forwards calls through a webhook, and stores every thread in a local database with a simple web inbox.
requirements: A telephony provider account with API access and a funded balance for numbers and per-message fees
A publicly reachable HTTPS URL for inbound webhooks, a cheap VPS or a tunnel works
A phone that can receive forwarded calls
Willingness to do carrier messaging registration if you send more than a trickle
whatYouLose: A real mobile app with push notifications, so texts arrive whenever you happen to open the browser
Number churn: burning and replacing numbers is one API call for you but a tidy flow in a product
MMS, group texts, voicemail transcription and call recording, each of which is its own build
Any pretense of an audited privacy story, since your logs, your database and your provider account are all pointed at you
Someone else handling carrier filtering, spam scoring and the paperwork when a number stops delivering
moatNotes: Numbers are a regulated, rented resource. You are always downstream of a carrier, whether you build this or buy it.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the value is not the inbox, it is the number supply and the fact that texts land on your phone without you thinking about it. Paying a few dollars a month for a maintained app beats keeping a webhook endpoint alive, watching a provider balance, and discovering at the worst moment that your DIY number got filtered into oblivion. If you need one throwaway number for a marketplace listing, the DIY build is fine and probably cheaper. If you rely on it for anything that matters, the subscription is buying you deliverability and someone to blame.
notes: Public detail on this one is thin, so treat the pricing and feature notes as unverified until someone checks. The build advice holds regardless: the app is easy, the telephony is rented.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted second-phone-number web app called "burnerbox".

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript, Tailwind for styling.
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, schema created on first boot, file at ./data/burnerbox.db.
- Twilio Node SDK for telephony. No other providers, no abstraction layer.
- Single user, no auth beyond a shared password from .env checked in middleware.

Secrets in .env only, with a .env.example committed:
TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID, TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN, PUBLIC_BASE_URL, FORWARD_TO_NUMBER, APP_PASSWORD.

Features in scope:
1. Numbers page: search available Twilio numbers by area code, buy one, list owned numbers, release a number with a confirm step. On purchase, set the voice and SMS webhooks to PUBLIC_BASE_URL routes automatically.
2. POST /api/webhooks/sms: verify the Twilio signature, store the inbound message, group by (owned number, counterparty number) into a thread.
3. POST /api/webhooks/voice: return TwiML that dials FORWARD_TO_NUMBER with the burner number as caller ID, and record nothing.
4. Inbox UI: thread list with last message preview and unread count, thread view, send a reply from the correct owned number.
5. Per-number label and notes so you remember why you bought it.

Explicitly out of scope: MMS, group messaging, voicemail, transcription, contacts import, mobile apps, push notifications, telemetry, analytics, any cloud service other than Twilio.

Deliverables: working app, README covering how to expose PUBLIC_BASE_URL for local dev with a tunnel, a note that Twilio charges per number and per message, and a note that sustained outbound messaging in the US requires A2P 10DLC registration or messages will be filtered.

Keep it under 15 files. Do not add a signup flow. Do not add a database migration framework.
